Subject: RFP: Audit logs — schema, exportability, preservation timeline (section 4)

Hi Irene,

Thanks for taking this RFP section. A few follow-ups from our security review team on audit/log retention and handoff. We're trying to understand what we can expect from Redwood if we select you as the inference provider. Please confirm the items below and attach any sample files you can share (schema, manifest, delivery examples).

Questions:
- Canonical audit record schema you can produce (fields, datatypes). Preferred formats: NDJSON, Parquet - can you deliver both?
- Retention windows by default and long-term preservation options (we need 7 years for certain record types).
- Ability to produce point-in-time exports for arbitrary date ranges (including incremental deltas).
- Packaging and tamper evidence: do you provide manifests, SHA256 hashes, signed manifests or chain-of-custody metadata?
- Support for redaction or masking of PII at export time vs. preserving original payload under legal hold.
- Typical timeline from request to delivery for a full handoff (including expedited options).

I've attached the RFP excerpt (Zephyr_RFP_section4_audit_requirements.pdf) with callouts. We need a written answer + sample manifest by the time your proposal is due (2026-11-12).

Best,
Emily
Emily Sanders
Head of Security Ops | Zephyr Finance

Subject: Re: RFP: Audit logs — schema, exportability, preservation timeline (section 4)

Hi Emily — thanks for the clear list. Quick ack and high-level responses below; I'm pulling a small cross-functional packet (schema, manifest sample, and a proposed preservation schedule) and will send the artifacts by EOD Wednesday. Can we also schedule a 30-minute technical call this week to walk the CISO team through the manifest and transfer options?

High-level answers: (short summary while we assemble attachments)
- Formats: We can produce NDJSON and Parquet exports natively.
- Retention: Default hot retention is 90 days; we support tiered archival (cold S3) and configurable long-term retention for up to 7+ years depending on contract.
- Point-in-time & deltas: yes — we support full-range exports and incremental (delta) packages using event-sequence cutoffs and manifest deltas.
- Tamper evidence: export bundles include per-file SHA256, a signed manifest (RSA 4096) and an optional notarized timestamp.
- Redaction: export-time redaction is supported for common PII classes; we also support sealed/complete exports for legal hold under a defined chain-of-custody.
- Timeline: standard handoff ~4–6 weeks; expedited 7–10 business days for scoped exports.

I'll attach a draft schema (redwood-auditlog-schema-v1.json) and a short sampling/preservation plan for your review.

Regards,
Irene Choi
Head of Solutions | Redwood Inference
irene.choi@redwood.ai | +1 650 555 0199

Attachments: redwood-auditlog-schema-v1.json, proposed-sampling-preservation-plan.xlsx

Date: Tue, 3 Nov 2026 09:18:00 -0800
Subject: Fwd: RFP: Audit logs — schema, exportability, preservation timeline (section 4)

Folks — forwarding Emily's request. Can you review and confirm the details below we should include in the final RFP response? I'm aiming for one coherent packet (schema + manifest example + timelines + S3/Snowball delivery options).

Key items to confirm/include in the packet:
- Canonical record fields: event_id (UUID), event_type, timestamp (ISO-8601 UTC), actor_id, actor_type (user/service), source_ip, request_id, request_payload_hash, response_hash, kv_meta (map), model_version, node_id, tenancy_id, retention_class
- Export formats: NDJSON and Parquet, with an export manifest (NDJSON) that enumerates each file, start_ts/end_ts, sha256, record_count, sequence_low/sequence_high.
- Delta exports: implement via sequence offsets (sequence_low/sequence_high) + manifest referencing base snapshot. This allows efficient rendezvous for incremental ingestion on the customer side.
- Tamper evidence: per-file SHA256 + manifest signed with Redwood private key (RSA-4096) + optional notarized timestamp from third-party time-stamping authority.
- Preservation timeline:
  * Operational (hot) storage: 90 days (default)
  * Warm archival (standard S3 IA): configurable 6 months — 3 years
  * Long-term retention: custom contract up to 7+ years, with periodic integrity checks every 90 days
- Sampling plan for expedited deliverable: if full export not feasible within timeframe, supply a deterministic sampling strategy (e.g., stratified by tenancy and event_type; seed provided to allow reproducible samples).
- Delivery options: presigned S3 + VPC peering transfer; SFTP over dedicated link; AWS Snowball for very large data sets; secure courier for physical media where required.
- Chain-of-custody: manifest, transfer logs, signature validation steps, and an optional notarized certificate.

Proposed timelines (for inclusion in RFP):
- Standard full export handoff (schema-conformant): 4–6 weeks from signed order + access verification
- Expedited scoped export: 7–10 business days (requires agreed scope and delivery method)
- For legal-hold sealed archives: timeline varies by volume; baseline 2–4 weeks to prepare sealed package and transfer keys

Marissa / Ben — please push any edits to the draft doc in the shared Drive link (https://drive.redwood.ai/shared/zephyr/audit-export-playbook) and I'll incorporate.

Irene

Thanks for the draft materials — good start. A few clarifications from our end before we publish your packet internally:

1) Can you confirm whether the event payload hash (request_payload_hash) is computed over the raw request body or the normalized (redacted/masked) body? For compliance we need to be able to verify integrity against the original request when under legal hold.
2) For delta exports, we need guarantee that sequence numbers are monotonic across tenant-level partitions. Is sequence_low/sequence_high global per tenant? Are gaps allowed?
3) Does the signed manifest include the public key fingerprint and key id? Our security team requires key rotation metadata.
4) We prefer transfer via S3 presigned + SSE-KMS; will you include KMS key id in the manifest? If Snowball is used, please confirm the expected handoff workflow and custody logs.

Also attaching our security profile for your reference. If you can respond to these four points in-line and update the manifest sample, we can proceed to the internal sign-off.

Emily

Subject: Re: RFP: Audit logs — schema, exportability, preservation timeline (section 4)

Emily — thank you, and good clarifications. Answers below (inline):

> 1) Can you confirm whether the event payload hash (request_payload_hash) is computed over the raw request body or the normalized (redacted/masked) body?

We compute request_payload_hash over the canonical raw request body at the time of ingestion (pre-redaction). For exports where redaction is requested, the manifest will include both the raw_payload_hash (for sealed/legal-hold exports) and exported_payload_hash (if the exported file has been redacted). Both hashes are included in the manifest so you can validate integrity against the sealed store.

> 2) For delta exports, we need guarantee that sequence numbers are monotonic across tenant-level partitions. Is sequence_low/sequence_high global per tenant? Are gaps allowed?

Sequence numbers are monotonic per tenant and per stream partition (we expose partition_id in the manifest). Gaps are possible only when records are deleted by retention policy or redaction; in such cases the manifest documents sequence gaps and includes a gap_reason field (e.g., retention_deletion, redaction_applied). For RFP purposes, we guarantee monotonicity in the active sequence space and provide explicit gap metadata.

> 3) Does the signed manifest include the public key fingerprint and key id? Our security team requires key rotation metadata.

Yes. Signed manifests include signing_key_id, signing_key_fingerprint (SHA256), and a signing_key_rotation_history reference (short ledger URL or blob id) so auditors can validate key lineage.

> 4) We prefer transfer via S3 presigned + SSE-KMS; will you include KMS key id in the manifest? If Snowball is used, please confirm the expected handoff workflow and custody logs.

We will include the KMS Key ID used for server-side encryption in the manifest when presigned S3 delivery is used. For Snowball: Redwood performs export to an encrypted Snowball device, we log the Snowball job id, shipping manifest, and transfer signatures; custody logs (transfer start/end, courier id, device id) are included in the chain-of-custody bundle.

Attached is an updated manifest sample (audit_manifest_sample.ndjson) showing raw_payload_hash AND exported_payload_hash fields, partition_id and gap_reason examples, and the signing_key metadata. Also included: a brief handoff checklist and the updated sampling/preservation plan.

Next steps:
- I'll upload the final packet to the Drive link.
- If this meets your needs we'll include the export SLA language and pricing appendix in the main proposal.
- Happy to join a 30-minute call with your CISO team tomorrow afternoon — let me know a time.

Best,
Irene Choi
Head of Solutions | Redwood Inference
